issue_context.title: Avoid computing `FormFeature` when calling `HttpRequest.HasFormContentType`
issue_context.body:
Currently, invoking the `HttpRequest.HasFormContentType` property will implicitly compute a `FormFeature` and use use that to compute whether the content type is form-related:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/76d2fda2659928859972211d99b5457180f2a8d8/src/Http/Http/src/Internal/DefaultHttpRequest.cs#L150-L153

We should consider updating this implementation such that it checks the content-type directly instead of allocating a feature.

cc: @davidfowl @Tratcher
comments: Just make sure the checks are consistent/equivalent. E.g. the alternative check you added in another recent PR was simplified for perf reasons and won't always return the same result.

> Just make sure the checks are consistent/equivalent. E.g. the alternative check you added in another recent PR was simplified for perf reasons and won't always return the same result.

Correct. I'd personally be fine with just calling [these methods](https://source.dot.net/#Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http/Features/FormFeature.cs,306) directly as a step towards optimization here.

I think we'd want to do a couple of investigations:
- Avoid allocating the MediaTypeHeader (see https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/376b6b0c860f113d59cf3e82677d7f8a6e674716/src/Mvc/Mvc.Core/src/Formatters/MediaType.cs)
- Avoid allocating the form feature if there isn't one already.
- This antiforgery check seems to happen when reading the form (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/376b6b0c860f113d59cf3e82677d7f8a6e674716/src/Http/Http/src/Features/FormFeature.cs#L77), which happens when you check the content type. This seems wrong.

review_comments:
Isn't this just checking for the presence of the form feature? If present, it should check the form feature's HasFormContentType.

The current form feature should also take precedence if it exists.
nit: I don't like that the ContentType property allocates a `MediaTypeHeaderValue`. IMO it should be a method.
The type is more reliable, methods just re-invent the parsers.

This is less precise / robust than the prior implementation. It's ok in the normal scenario, but it can cause strange random bugs for other inputs. E.g. this now matches "web-application/x-www-form-urlencoded-foo".

We have tools that can get the same precision as before without allocating:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/src/Shared/MediaType/ReadOnlyMediaTypeHeaderValue.cs

> We have tools that can get the same precision as before without allocating:

Ah, perfect! This is exactly what I was looking for.
